cards.text: Proverbs is the wisdom of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel (Prov 1:1). Here he's talking to someone he calls my son, and he opens with a big if: if you've put up security for your neighbor, if you've shaken hands on a pledge with a stranger. Friend, I know that handshake. That's the 'what could possibly go wrong' handshake.

cards.question: Solomon says that after a pledge like that, the son is caught in a trap. What trapped him?

answers.text: The words of his own mouth
A thief hiding by the road
A debt his father left him

cards.text: Solomon says the son has fallen into his neighbor's hands. Worst place to fall, friend. I'd rather fall face-first into the chocolate chips. Actually, I have. Many times.

cards.question: To get free, Solomon tells the son to go to his neighbor, ___ himself, and press his plea.
True or false: Solomon tells the son this can wait until he's had a good night's sleep.

cards.text: No sleep for the eyes, no slumber for the eyelids. This is not a snooze-button problem, friend. This is a one-sock-on, keys-in-your-teeth, out-the-door problem.

cards.question: Solomon tells the son to free himself like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler. What's he telling the son to do?

answers.text: Get loose quickly while he still can
Hide quietly until the trouble passes
Turn and fight whoever set the trap

cards.text: Then Solomon calls out somebody new: the slacker. And he hands the slacker a teacher straight from the animal world.

cards.question: Which creature does Solomon tell the slacker to learn from?

cards.text: Solomon says to observe its ways and become wise. A grown person, sent to take notes from a BUG. Hey, I once took life advice from a dead battery in my old junk drawer, so who am I to talk?

cards.question: True or false: The ant has a commander standing over it, making sure it gets its work done.
The ant prepares its provisions in summer and gathers its food at harvest. What makes that so wise?

answers.text: It gets ready before it needs to
It saves food for other creatures
It rests once the work is done

cards.text: Then Solomon turns back to the slacker, who is STILL lying there. "How long will you lie there, O slacker? When will you get up from your sleep?" Friend, I lay in a drawer for YEARS, and I didn't even have a choice. Get UP.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the slacker's trouble starts with one big, long nap.

cards.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest. Little. Little. Little. That's how it gets you, friend. Nobody ever says, "I'm about to ruin my life." They say, "Five more minutes."

cards.question: All that little rest adds up. Solomon says poverty will come upon the slacker like a ___.

cards.text: Poverty like a robber, need like a bandit. Think about it, friend. Nobody puts the robber on their calendar.
New picture now. Solomon describes a worthless person, a wicked man who walks around with a perverse mouth.

cards.question: This wicked man doesn't only talk with his mouth. What else does he talk with?

answers.text: His eyes and feet and fingers
Songs and riddles at the gate

cards.text: Winking his eyes. Speaking with his feet. Pointing with his fingers. This man is a whole group chat, and he's typing with his ENTIRE body.

cards.question: With deceit in his heart, the wicked man devises evil and keeps sowing ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon says therefore. Everything this man has been planting is about to come up.

cards.question: What does Solomon say will come upon the wicked man?

answers.text: A slow and quiet decline over time

cards.text: In an instant, shattered beyond recovery. That's a cookie hitting a tile floor, friend. There is no five-second rule for THAT.
Then Solomon gives a list: six things the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him. Lean in, friend. This one matters.

cards.question: The LORD's list starts with the eyes. He hates ___ eyes.
True or false: A lying tongue is on the list of things the LORD hates.
Next, the LORD's list gets to the hands. What kind of hands does He hate?

cards.text: Eyes. Tongue. Hands. The list is working its way right down the body.

cards.question: The LORD also hates a ___ that devises wicked schemes, and ___ that run swiftly to evil.

cards.text: Number six on the list: a false witness who gives false testimony. One more to go.

cards.question: What's number seven, the last thing on the LORD's list?

answers.text: One who stirs up discord among brothers
One who turns away from the poor
One who breaks a promise to a friend

cards.text: Discord again. The wicked man was busy sowing it, and now it closes out the LORD's whole list. So friend, if your hobby is starting drama, this is NOT the shout-out you were hoping for.
